newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Dev hits high ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: New World Dev hits high ahead of results.

text.p: Shares of blue-chip property group New World Development Co Ltd rose to an all-time high of HK$47.80 per share in mid morning on Monday before edging back, boosted by expectations of strong year earnings, brokers said.
New World shares, which gained HK$2.30 or 5.26 percent last week, were up HK$1.60 or 3.48 percent to HK$47.60.
The firm is due to release fiscal 1996 results on Thursday.
"Anticipation of strong earnings growth fuelled demand especially because many of its projects have started contributing to profit," said Dennis Leung, property analyst at Dharmala Securities.
Analysts said the concensus forecast was for net profit growth of 26 percent to HK$4.31 billion.

Shares in New World Development have risen 7.73 percent since mid-October, when the company launched a convertible bond issue, raising capital to fund its property development and investment activities in China.
Last week, New World raised the sum of the 4.00 percent mandatorily convertible bond issue to US$350 million from HK$300 million to cover over-allotment.

"I think definitely the recent excitement is a result of the CB (convertible bond) issue on its China properties. I think the market just basically was surprised by the strong and also massive presence of New World in the PRC," said Nicholas Wong, property analyst at HSBC James Capel.
Analysts said the share price now looked fairly valued following the recent rise and further upside was limited.
